 Follow Two Texas VA employees accused of fraud, theft by DOJ
 Bill Eaves Tue, November 17, 2026 at 9:44 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. NCM Two Department of Veterans Affairs employees in Texas face federal charges in separate schemes involving diverted disability payments and inflated delivery fees for medical equipment, the Justice Department announced Tuesday.
 RELATED: Odem "Hometown Hero" laid to rest with procession parade 
 The cases involve a Houston VA Medical Center employee accused in a scheme that allegedly defrauded the agency of about $182,000 and a VA National Call Center employee in Killeen accused of redirecting veterans' benefits to a bank account she controlled.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the Houston case, Yolanda Johnson Sayed, 61, was charged by criminal information with conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
 According to the charging document, Sayed worked as a prosthetics representative and conspired with the owner of a VA-approved vendor to direct purchase orders to the company and approve inflated delivery charges. The purchases involved mobility equipment, including wheelchairs and walkers.
 Prosecutors allege Sayed used government-issued purchase cards to pay fraudulent invoices and received a share of the proceeds through electronic transfers.
 Between November 2020 and August 2025, she allegedly conducted about 1,437 transactions with the vendor. The government is seeking forfeiture of at least $182,000 in alleged fraud proceeds.
 Advertisement Advertisement In the Killeen case, an indictment alleges Heidi Brady used her position at the VA National Call Center to access veterans' information and divert disability payments.
 Prosecutors allege Brady used information obtained through her interactions with veterans, along with her knowledge of VA payment procedures, to change their direct deposit information shortly before monthly benefits were issued. The payments then went to a bank account she controlled, according to the indictment.
 The Justice Department's announcement did not specify how much money Brady allegedly diverted or how many veterans were affected.
 "When somebody defrauds the VA, they are stealing from the honorable men and women who have served this nation and from the taxpayers who fund a collective commitment to support our veterans," said U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.
 Advertisement Advertisement The Texas cases were included in a nationwide enforcement effort targeting VA benefits fraud and related offenses. The Justice Department said the effort resulted in charges against 15 defendants involving more than $3.4 million in alleged intended losses between Sept. 1 and Nov. 17.
 Federal prosecutors also announced the creation of the Texas Federal Fraud Task Force, bringing together all four U.S. attorney's offices in Texas with support from federal, state and local law enforcement to combat fraud across the state.
